clinicalPearls: A rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by loss-of-function variants in SLC2A2, which encodes the glucose transporter GLUT2 expressed in liver, pancreatic beta cells, intestine and the renal proximal tubule
It combines hepatorenal glycogen accumulation with a generalised proximal (Fanconi-type) renal tubulopathy
Typical features are hepatomegaly, failure to thrive, a doll-like face and rickets from renal phosphate and bicarbonate wasting
A characteristic paradoxical glucose profile is seen: fasting hypoglycaemia together with postprandial hyperglycaemia and glucosuria
The proximal tubulopathy produces glycosuria, generalised aminoaciduria, phosphaturia, bicarbonate wasting with proximal renal tubular acidosis and low-molecular-weight proteinuria
Growth retardation and rickets often dominate the clinical picture and require attention to phosphate, alkali and vitamin D
Massive glucosuria persists despite hypoglycaemia because impaired GLUT2 blocks tubular glucose exit into the blood
reference.pathophysiology: Fanconi-Bickel syndrome results from biallelic loss-of-function variants in SLC2A2, encoding the facilitative glucose transporter GLUT2. GLUT2 mediates the movement of glucose across the basolateral membrane of hepatocytes, pancreatic beta cells, enterocytes and proximal tubular cells. Its deficiency traps glucose within these cells, causing glycogen accumulation in liver and kidney and disturbing glucose sensing and homeostasis, which manifests as fasting hypoglycaemia with postprandial hyperglycaemia. In the proximal tubule, failure of basolateral glucose exit, together with the intracellular glycogen burden, impairs reabsorptive function broadly, producing a generalised Fanconi syndrome with glycosuria, aminoaciduria, phosphaturia and bicarbonate wasting, and the consequent phosphate loss and acidosis drive rickets and growth failure.
additionalDifferentials: Cystinosis and other causes of renal Fanconi syndrome
Other glycogen storage disorders with hepatomegaly and hypoglycaemia
additionalInvestigations: Fasting and postprandial blood glucose to demonstrate the paradoxical pattern
Assessment of proximal tubular function including glucose, amino acids, phosphate, bicarbonate and low-molecular-weight proteinuria
Liver imaging and function tests to assess hepatomegaly and glycogen accumulation
Skeletal assessment for rickets with measurement of phosphate, alkaline phosphatase and vitamin D metabolites
Monitoring of growth and acid-base and electrolyte status
redFlags: Severe metabolic acidosis or electrolyte disturbance from tubular losses
Progressive rickets with skeletal deformity or fracture
Significant failure to thrive or dehydration during intercurrent illness
reference.prognosis: With supportive management of hypoglycaemia, electrolyte and phosphate losses, acidosis and rickets, growth and metabolic control can improve and many patients do reasonably well, although short stature and osteopenia may persist; kidney function is often relatively preserved compared with other proximal tubulopathies.
pitfalls: Being confused by the paradoxical fasting hypoglycaemia with postprandial hyperglycaemia and misclassifying the glucose disorder
Failing to correct phosphate, alkali and vitamin D, leaving rickets undertreated
Overlooking the generalised tubulopathy when hepatomegaly dominates the presentation
Attributing persistent glucosuria to diabetes rather than proximal tubular glucose loss
management: Prevent fasting hypoglycaemia with frequent feeds and slow-release carbohydrate such as uncooked cornstarch, while restricting free galactose and simple sugars
Replace ongoing proximal tubular losses with oral phosphate supplements and alkali such as bicarbonate or citrate to correct the proximal renal tubular acidosis
Treat rickets with active vitamin D metabolites such as calcitriol or alfacalcidol alongside phosphate supplementation
Correct and monitor electrolyte disturbances including hypokalaemia and maintain adequate hydration
Monitor growth, acid-base status, electrolytes and skeletal health regularly
Refer to metabolic medicine, nephrology and paediatric dietetics for coordinated care
Provide genetic counselling and family screening given autosomal recessive SLC2A2 inheritance
